title: Rent and the City

# Why rents rise

Rents rise when **demand** outpaces *supply*, and the gap is __not__ closing.

## What the data says

- Vacancy fell in every borough.
- New building slowed:
    - permits were down;
    - completions lagged.

1. First, wages stalled.
2. Second, costs climbed.

> A city that cannot house its workers will not keep them.
